Thanks, Sofia — helpful start. I pulled together a first-pass rooming draft and a couple of operational constraints below. Please use the attached spreadsheet as the working file and update as you confirm arrivals.

Operational constraints / asks (Redwood):
- Please keep the 7 VIPs on the 12th floor (adjacent suites) and assign single rooms. VIP list to follow.
- Quiet-floor preference: two execs (CTO + Head of Product) require low-traffic rooms and white-noise machines.
- Pair managers with at least one direct where possible (for after-hours sync).
- We will take a partial master bill for meeting spaces and F&B; guest rooms will be charged to individuals unless otherwise noted.
- Staggered check-in: prefer split windows (10am–1pm, 2pm–6pm) for the larger groups to reduce front-desk congestion.

I uploaded a draft rooming matrix (rooming_draft.xlsx). Key columns: Attendee, Title, Arrival, Departure, Room type, Roommate preference, Special needs.

Attachments: rooming_draft.xlsx (xlsx, 24KB)

- Quiet-block: CTO and Head of Product assigned to rooms 1203 & 1205; white-noise machines requested.
- Master bill: Redwood will accept a partial master bill covering meeting rooms, F&B for plenary sessions, and block shuttle costs. Guest rooms remain on individuals except CTO suite.
- Check-in windows: 10:00–13:00 and 14:00–18:00. Late concierge scheduled 21:00–00:00 for red-eye arrivals.
- Building access: Laura will provide final name list for badges by Wednesday, Jun 16 12:00pm PT.

Next steps:
- Sofia: please update the rooming_draft.xlsx with confirmed flight times and mark the five international transfers.
- Oliver / Gravitas: confirm cars for VIPs and shuttle schedule by Thursday.
- Marissa & Monica: mark dietary codes in the final matrix and confirm master bill line items.

If you agree with the above, reply with a brief ACK and any objections. I will push the finalized CSV to the hotel and send the access list to security after we have two ACKs.
